nodes.label: docs/canon/USER_CANON.md — what the user actually said, verbatim, organised by subject: the design canon (Part I, §1–13), the working-relationship canon (Part II, §14–23), a dated timeline of decisions and reversals (Part III), and what was never built or never answered (Part IV). Every line inside a quote is his own text, spelling and profanity intact; contradictions are preserved and named, never resolved. Interpretation, produced 2026-08-03 and unreviewed: the quotes are verbatim intent, but which were selected, how they were grouped and what the headings call them are agent judgement, and 141 entries are second-hand [DOC] recoveries rather than chat.

What this covers, and the source class every quote carries. Verbatim human turns: the corpus is 920, 2026-05-14T12:30:48Z → 2026-08-05T14:43:34Z, desktop 127 + laptop 793, merged — while this document's quote selection was made against the 803-turn snapshot that existed on 08-03 (desktop 127 + laptop 676), and the 117 turns added since are in raw/user_turns_all.jsonl and have not been swept into these sections. Second-hand recovered rulings: 80 labelled rulings plus ~150 verbatim quotes from 20 agent-written design docs, 05-25 → 07-12. Git: 74 commits, 2026-05-07 → 2026-08-01, 91 reproduce commands, 18 numbered contradictions. The classes: [CHAT] from raw/user_turns_all.jsonl, his own keystrokes, first-hand and timestamped, the primary source and the highest trust; [DOC] recovered from an agent-written design or state doc that quoted him, second-hand and reliable to the extent that agent transcribed accurately, with the 06-28 design-evolution doc strongest because it cites [tNN] turn numbers; [COMMIT] his own commit message, first-hand but terse; and [TOOL-RESULT — absent from the corpus], his answer to an AskUserQuestion prompt quoted from the session transcript and cited by session file, record line and UTC timestamp — first-hand keystrokes, but not reachable through user_turns_all.jsonl. Verbatim only: every line inside a quote is his own text, spelling and profanity intact, nothing smoothed or paraphrased, and where a section needs interpretation it appears on a line beginning "Reading:" and never inside a quote. Contradictions are preserved, not resolved: where he said one thing and later the opposite, both appear in date order and the reversal is named.

What this canon cannot tell you. Nothing before 2026-05-14 exists as chat: the project's first commit is 2026-05-07, and the whole first week — the initial 52-file Neo4j pipeline, the 12-entry decision log, the original graph schema, the controlled canonical vocabulary — survives only in git and in the design docs, with no transcript anywhere. Two chat blackouts: 05-16 → 05-26, 11 days, zero human turns on either machine; and 05-29 → 06-26, 29 days, zero human turns on either machine. Those two windows contain the entire v2 pivot, the facet redesign, the closing of the graph spine, the death of the chunk description, the build gate, the eval-harness design and the RAGAS-only purge — and they are not lost: they are covered second-hand by the [DOC] record (20 docs dated 05-25, 05-31, 06-03, 06-04, 06-09, 06-11, 06-12, 06-14, 06-18, 06-23, 06-25 ×3, 06-28 ×3, 07-01, 07-12) and by git. The correction to a claim in circulation: these windows do not "have no records of any kind" — they have no chat and a substantial doc record, so [DOC] is second-hand, not absent. Thin days are thin, not silent: 05-27 and 05-28 carry one turn each, 07-02 two, 07-12 three, 07-27 two, and absence of a statement on a date proves nothing. Every answer he gave through an AskUserQuestion prompt is missing from the corpus: tools/canon_extract.py discards a user record the moment it carries a tool_result block (classify, the rule at lines 118-121) — 2,530 records in the laptop pass — so "there is no turn for it" does not mean he never said it. Four such records exist and each is a decision: 2026-07-30T23:10:40.745Z (how tags inform the interpretation), 2026-08-02T09:32:26.648Z (chunk position in cluster space; rank-aware metrics first), 2026-08-05T11:39:56.193Z (no framing — report the statistics), 2026-08-05T13:48:50.008Z (flag-gated derivation). An earlier agent called 2026-07-15 "the first day" of the project — the earliest date in one partial local extract, wrong by two months; his reply: "Day one? 2 weeks ago.. you ARE retarded.." ([CHAT] 08-02). Do not repeat it.

The pre-chat era is in git — go read it. The design history of the blackout weeks is written down in commits, diffs, code and docs, and these are the design-era record, 2026-05-07 → 2026-06-28. dba1160 (05-07) initial commit, 52 files, the full Neo4j indexing pipeline, docs/architecture.md with its 12-entry decision log, docs/graph_schema.md at 280 lines. 48fbc9d (05-11) "rename cluster dimensions" → theme→topic, object_entity→entities, event_process→activity, time_relevance→temporal, information_need→evidence. 399ee32 (05-13) "Rework HERB chunking and tagging frames", which also silently deletes the canonical vocabulary. 415148d (05-14) documents the HERB query interpretation layer. 4ab34b4 (05-15) the only commit that ever carried Claude memory files. 54bc1a4 (05-28) v1 as shipped — retrieval.ts, the seven-factor scoreCypher and its five hard gates. 296fc40 (05-30) v2 artefact-rebuild design, shape-probe prototype, NVIDIA host verification. 18d11df (06-01) reference-resolver prototype and the §13 semantic-dimensions research. 0efff16 (06-15) "Separate repo into v1/ (frozen) and v2/ (active)", +750 design lines, the largest single design landing and the first CLAUDE.md. 28c95aa (06-24) the v3/artefact subsystem — DESIGN.md, MODEL_CONTRACTS.md, keys/Salesforce__HERB.yaml. 8a640bf (06-28) titled "update graphify-out (533 files)", actually shipping artefact/tag.py, chunk.py, the 659-line facet-derivation survey, and deleting v3/eval/herb.py. 69115e0 (07-12) titled "update graphify-out (49 files)", actually introducing v3/pipelines/artefact_v1.py, the arm producing every reported artefact number. origin/jockedev2 (05-19) six unmerged RAGAS commits squashed into 5706520 with an empty body, the only surviving record of "Effect is question-type-dependent — not a general graph win." Branches carrying them: origin/djuret/monorepo (real impl and docs, paths under backend/), v3 (holds the frozen v1/), v3_artefact_build. The current branch has been cleared of old material — the working tree is not the record. Read with git show <ref>:<path>; also git log --all -S'<term>' --name-only and git log --all --format='%ad %h %s' --date=short.

How to re-derive this: python tools/canon_extract.py, which writes docs/canon/raw/ — user_turns_all.jsonl / .md (the corpus), rejected_sample*.md (what the filter threw out and why), and EXTRACT_REPORT*.md (counts, per-rule reject tallies, and the false-negative audit of the harness_template rule: 0 of 6,380). The desktop half is merged in from OneDrive\Coding\state-transfer\GRAG-Job\_desktop_transcripts. docs/canon/raw/ is read-only: do not edit it, re-derive instead. The standing instruction that produced the file, all [CHAT] 08-02: "have you fucking done ANYTHING based on actual canon? i fucking demand you filter through every fucking memory and chatlog you have and find out everything I HAVE SAID, THOROUGHLY"; "Search the entire repo for exactly ALL information I (the user, fucking ME) i have conveyed, the actual things I ACTUALLY SAID: all conversations, memories, logs, docs, data, diffs, committs, changes, fixes and code.. that means you have to search the entire git-repo also with all the fucking branches etc, this is not a small job, but it is the most important one we have ever done here."; and "THE GODDAMN GIT REPO HAS ALL THE FUCKING HISTORY SPOKEN IN COMMITS, DIFFS , CODE and DOCS.. what the actual fuck is wrong with you?"

§1 the artefact's intended construction. The single fullest statement of the v1 concept in the whole corpus, [CHAT] 07-06: "so, it was file -> chunks -> tags. the chunks reference the files, the chunks contain a short description of the chunk, a relational weight of the chunk to the file, tags with relational values of the tags to the chunk, and then the tags have the facet-values too. Pretty much all of this is embedded, the chunk description, the tagsnames, the facets etc.. meaning, in the actual graph, there are no 'content' like that, just a bunch of related embeddings.. and the interpretor does it's thing with the input like getting facetvalues/rankings of the prompt, a description of the prompt which can be embedded and checked vs chunk-description-embeddings and so on… The tags themselves are embedded, meaning we have an embedding as the actual tag". Around it: the facet program's origin, "the point of the multifacets was to give the tag a more semantical weight and direction with the facets" ([DOC] 05-25); "Measure from embeddings (IF POSSIBLE) is way better than more prompting" and "measure from embeddings was my idea" ([DOC] 06-09); "it took so fucking long to get it right and it still didn't work at all" on v1's model-emitted weights ([DOC] 06-11); "combinations of solutions are the trick" ([DOC] 06-28 [t14]); "an optimal solution would to NOT have all of this in the graph, intead do it live-prompt-time" ([DOC] 06-28 [t52]); "the actual content should never exist in the graph at all, and we fixed that by just making pointers again" ([CHAT] 07-06); "facets are on 1 edge" and "there are only 5 faces, just fucking put them on the fucking edge" ([CHAT] 07-06); and "you are both bastardizing and forgetting the origins, those are my thoughts defiled, the origial concepts were mine" ([CHAT] 07-21). On the published abstract other people wrote about the work he ruled twice: "i do prefer if we can keep it somewhat close" ([CHAT] 06-30) and "those that wrote that does not FULLY know what we are doing, so that is not canon, just an assumption" ([CHAT] 07-21). Reading: three distinct systems get called "the artefact" in this record and mixing them is the single most common agent error in the corpus — (a) original v1, the thesis-era browser/Neo4j build of the k=40 era on old branches; (b) current artefact_v1, the Python arm in v3/pipelines/ running over the same herb-eval graph with a new retrieval engine; (c) the v3 artefact, the unfinished native rebuild under v3/artefact/. The 07-26 turn is the authoritative disambiguation.

§2 the graph, and using it as a graph. The node/attribute rule in his own words, all [DOC] 06-12: "if we are saying file -> chunk ->tags .. where are those OTHER RANDOM FUCKING NODES!?"; "either they are nodes, but then we get edges to EVERY fucking chunk, or they are just attributes… perhaps it's smarter to just have shit like that as attributes on chunks"; "that sounds a bit fucked up to have them as nodes, most of them will be a chunk, meaning we have 2 almost same nodes"; "that has the potential to put a fuckton of data into the graph, both GDPR data, and not — why not just have the parent field as the connection and when searched for, you can find anna"; "it's dead, such shit is 'interpreter area'", killing minted facet-label hub nodes; and "where the fuck in the graph do you think this is?" on an agent proposing to search field values in the graph. The line he has repeated in some form ever since, [CHAT] 06-30: "yeah i really think this should be nodes or edges so to speak etc, half the strength of of a graph is beeing able to route/search based on relationships instead of structures", with the generality clause "Dont think herb, think dataset agnostic concept" ([CHAT] 07-01). Also here: "just some thoughts btw, thinking about the actual size of the graph here, is there a reason to have the phrases in there? shouldnt we just embed them and put the embedding as a node in the graph instead with the reference just like the phrase would have?" ([DOC] 06-28 [t68]); and the multihop question, "if we build the graph correctly, wont it emulate/do multihop natively purely by design?" ([CHAT] 07-15). Reading: "is the graph being used as a graph?" is asked on 06-30, 07-15, 07-20, 07-21, 07-28, 07-29 and 08-02 — seven times across five weeks, never answered to his satisfaction.

§3 tags — what they are and what they are for. The purpose statement, said twice on the same day in two sessions, [CHAT] 07-30: "you and every other agent seem to be missing that the whole fucking point of the tags, is guiding to the correct gold-bearing chunks" and "i was under the impression that we did the whole fucking tag-clustering and facets and weights just to fucking guide it all to the correct chunks, why the absolute fuck was this NOT done then?". Same day: "ok, so we make sure it is informed by the tags first then, as IT WAS FUCKING INTENDED from the start" and "descriptions in every tag was an abomination and should never have been there, i am still angry abou tthat". Earlier: no LLM judge in the creation of tags or facets in the graph ([CHAT] 06-27); "do our fucking tags have values or not?" ([CHAT] 07-21). On 08-02, the tag layer's construction and its pollution: "tell me EXACTLY, verbatim, how the tag-layer works now, how it is built, used, calculated"; "Hapax?" and "hapax would let them matter more because of vectorisation?"; "Eh.. what..we have tags with that fucking syntax? For real?"; "but those you just showed me.. those are tags!?"; and "this is a retagged variant also? this is not the db we did the 'purge' on, right?"

§3 reversal — "tags first" was said, then the implementation of it was rejected. On 07-30 he asked to make it "informed by the tags first … as IT WAS FUCKING INTENDED from the start". What was built was a tag-reachability regime (HERB_TAG_FIRST) in which tags gate membership. On 08-01 he rejected exactly that: "ITS NT SUPPOSED TO BE FUCKING TAG REACHABLE ffs.. tags are supposed to INFORM/weight the chunks" ([CHAT] 08-01). Reading: "tags first" means tags weight and inform earliest and hardest in the ordering. It does not mean tags decide which chunks are eligible. Those are different mechanisms and only the first is canon.

§4 facets. The origin statement: facets exist to "give the tag a more semantical weight and direction" ([DOC] 05-25). Why the model cannot produce them: an LLM cannot put correct weights on tags or chunks, so measure from embeddings instead ([DOC] 06-09), with his v1 evidence "it took so fucking long to get it right and it still didn't work at all". Where they live: all facet weights on ONE edge, the chunk→tag edge, five of them ([CHAT] 07-06). The multi-step relevance concept: tag-facets inform the RELEVANCE of the tag, per facet, relative to its chunk, so the facet weight multiplies the tag's chunk-relevance weight, both baked, steered at query time by the interpreter's facet ranking ([CHAT] 06-27). A mechanism he floated himself: per-facet centrality — "perhaps we can do that, but based on each facet! giving a relational value of the tag to its siblings based on each facet!?" ([DOC] 06-11). On combining them, objections and none of them a ruling: "specifically multiplication i am not sold on" ([DOC] 05-25). Then five weeks of asking what the facets are actually doing, ending in "wait, what is affecting the interpreter from the facets that actually changes the response/interpretation?" ([CHAT] 07-25).

§4 THE FACET REVERSALS — three of them, all his own. F1, what a facet is: three positions, each superseding the last — 06-14 "relevance weights, not interpretation", a facet as the relevance coordinate or character of a tag; 06-25 "I think we should separate tag facets and routing" / "the v1 facets were actual semantic meaning around the tag", a facet as a semantic description of the phrase with routing a separate downstream consumer, which kills the 06-14 framing eleven days later; and 06-27 "you HAVE to remember that the facets are themed RELEVANCE weights.. meaninig you have to think about them differently, like info-kind and entity-type (are they even facets..?)", a facet as a graded how-much dial, which re-kills the 06-25 framing. F2, entity-type and information-kind — out, in, out: out on 05-30 in an agent allocation table later disowned, with entities/temporal/evidence relocated to hard fields as "the v1 junk facets"; back in on 06-25, "Would not the old facets work with the new tags? (not the weighting, the concept)", the distinction he drove being fact-vs-kind — the eid is structure, the kind of information is meaning; and out again on 06-27, a thing that answers "which" is not a facet because a facet must be graded. The reconciliation between this and the 06-28 categorical framing was recorded as an open problem and never closed. F3, one edge per facet → all facets on one edge: v1 shipped an edge per facet; on 06-09 he asked "weren't we supposed to have ALL the facet weights on the SAME edge!?"; on 06-25 he stated the original intent was misread, "'one edge per facet' was just bad communication... they were supposed to be on the same fucking edge"; and on 07-06 he closed it flatly, "there are only 5 faces, just fucking put them on the fucking edge". This one is settled and does not reopen.

§5 clustering, cluster-K, levels of k's, fuzzy cutoffs. The pre-v1 instinct: "the first tought was to use clustering based on the facets as a 'filter/router' amongst the tags etc" ([CHAT] 06-27), and "that was before i started building v1". "i mean, i really do like the concept of clustering tags/weights on facets based on the prompts values" ([DOC] 06-28 [t49]). The geometry definition, [CHAT] 07-21: "no dude, ITS A FUCKING CLUSTERING, why are you doing rankings and countings!? its the fucking embeddings distances vs eachothers and those distances are the fucking clusters, holy shit", with "why did you make up a number like 200 here? dont you know how knn works at all?" beside it. The cluster-K definition, [CHAT] 07-21: "if they are already affecting which things are put in the retrieval and in what order isnt this just an issue with us not cutting off at a good cluster-k value? my thought with the clustering was that we get that curve of best fit and let that decide the correct K for that solution". The fullest specification in the corpus, [CHAT] 07-31: "1. i THINK it might be smartest to compute the clusters at build, and then weight-adjust them based on the query's facet-values.. i THINK, reflect on this with me.. 2. something like that, i used best fit as the fuzzy cutoff-point for the cluster's edges tho, aka the size of the cluster or what will you, but perhaps the query-adjustment comes first before what the best fit is for this query". Also: per-facet clusterings for semantically different clusters (07-31); "wasnt the plan to cluster the tags weighted by facets in combination with chunk-descriptions to find the best fit of chunks?" (08-02); "i dont think the walk and the 'best fit' is helping eachother, you?" (07-22); and the standing distrust of the state doc written that day. REVERSAL — when the clusters are computed: "the clusters are based on the actual shit from the prompt, so you cant pre-run it..?" (07-21) against "compute the clusters at build, and then weight-adjust them" (07-31), ten days apart, opposite positions, both hedged by him ("..?", "i THINK", "reflect on this with me"). Neither is a ruling; do not treat either as settled.

§5 Reading — the vocabulary, and who owns which word. Fuzzy clustering, levels of k's, query-relative areas, cluster-K, and best fit as the fuzzy cutoff are the user's terms. NNK pruning, gap cut, RRF / fusion arrangement, and value knee are agent coinages he explicitly did not name, invent, or accept. When an agent uses one of the second set as if it were the design, that is the failure he named on 07-20: "you keep saying things i am unsure of, have not really accepted and just fucking exist there, like the nkk pruning, fusion arrengement, gap cut.. NONE of these are something i named or invented, what the fuck are they?"

§6 retrieval shape — guidance, not filtering. The four-point rejection of the gate, [CHAT] 07-15, the most-cited retrieval ruling in the corpus: "1. gate? wtf? why have a gate? why not ust that as promoted guidance? or am i missing something here? hard filter seems insane, much better to use rankings etc, taht way we can use both better k of hits and maybe even clustering of areas to increase to if hits are weak etc.. 2. 10? fucking why just 10? 3. use of the defect solution 4. only on NOTHING? fuck this is also retarded — Honestly, no fucking wonder we get shit results, this is an abomination." On matching: multiple literal hits produce boosts only, never removal ([DOC] 06-12); "thinking humans write correctly, is naive as fuck, ESPECIALLY when talking to an llm" and "exact + fuzzy IS the way to go for herb" ([DOC] 06-12); "i mean by fuzzy i actually mean embedded" and "cant we just do the evaluation-curve for the ranking of those 'exponential', we dont have to decide the actual angle now, but kinda meaning 'exact = max' on that curve" ([CHAT] 06-30). On ordering: "isnt scope and description supposed to be a guiding prio 'if they fit' so to speak?" (07-23); "all of them.. why the fuck are you guys not understanding this fucking concept?" on which parts must matter in the ordering (07-25); and "no, the part that reshapes the fucking prompt into a description THE FUCKING DESCRIPTIONS DUDE" (07-29). Attribution note: the 05-31 handoff's "NO hard filters anywhere (strong user stance)" and the 05-25 recall → filter → rank → cap shape are attributed to him as rulings but reproduce nothing he typed, so they carry no [DOC] tag — his own words on the same rule are the 07-15 four-point rejection. The agentic-retrieval idea he raised and parked himself, [CHAT] 07-21: "arent all arms here kinda supposed to be available as 'tool calls' for the llm … ours it can be a bit more active with" and "what i am after here, is letting the agent actually 'hold on to the conversation' so to speak and decide when it has the informtion to answer the question", closed by "dude, it's the same fucking thing, but we let the interpreter do it now.. so.. whatever.."

§7 arbitrary numbers. The rule, [CHAT] 07-15: "i do NOT like arbitrary choices for k or any number or value, fucking BASE it on something, i kinda like knn clustering for relevance spheres for example for grounding, k, retrival etc etc", said the same day as "2. 10? fucking why just 10?". Restated 07-21 ("why did you make up a number like 200 here?") and 08-02 ("arbitrarily decided hard limits, like the 64 chunk limit, i bet there is way more than 1 of these dumb limits lying around not beeing seen"). Reading: the standing objection has two halves and both are load-bearing — (a) a constant must be derived from something in the data, not chosen; and (b) a pre-registered pass/fail bar invented by an agent is itself an arbitrary number, so 07-31 rejects the bar, not the measurement.

§8 overfitting, and keeping agents blind to the gold. "by NOT overfitting it to the specific dataset we have" ([CHAT] 06-30); "it's VERY important that this is not overfitted to the specific dataset because you make it sound like you are doing exactly that" (07-15); "we obviously cannot overfit, i want a smart AND clean solution" (07-22); and the 08-02 verdict "not only did i mean you are forcing an architecture BASED on retrieving the gold based on the questions, it also feels like you are focusing on it". The mechanism he named, [CHAT] 08-02: "honestly, you should not have the questions/gold available to you, there is 0% good that can come out of taht" and "can we make sure 'you' never see them? that you only get the variable/pointer to it?". Reading: this is why v3/data/questions.jsonl, gold100.jsonl, heldout100.jsonl and 10smoke.jsonl must not be opened by an agent doing design work — the constraint is about the designer seeing the answers, not about the code reading them at runtime.

§9 evaluation, metrics, and what the score is and is not for. The scorer decision and its reversal seven days later: "no, i am saying we do both" — HERB anchor plus RAGAS lens ([DOC] 06-18) — then "this is ONLY RAGAS" said twice on 06-25, with eval/herb.py deleted; the consequence, that every number this project reports is RAGAS-only and none is comparable to HERB's published leaderboard, is accepted by him. Standing rulings: k ≠ top-k, with k the global ceiling identical for every arm and top-k each arm's actual return under it; k = 50; gold-100, never --set full; the four judged metrics; structured generator outputs. Gathering the data: "i WANT TO GATHER ALL THE DATA, stop fucking around, this is an academic effort" (06-27), no interpretation and no curve substitutes; full metrics including split in/out tokens because build data matters for traceability and reproducibility (07-16); metric selection is his call, never an agent's (07-29). The benchmark itself, matched budget and the unit problem — which he found himself: "k=50 does not mean the same for all arms, and thats retarded.. how did the true v1 runs measure it?" and "perhaps K shouldnt be chunks, perhaps we should put a max token budget instead" (07-26). The 90%-air problem (07-29). Held-out generalization: a new evenly-distributed 100q set, not the 800, all-answerable required, read afterwards as "pretty much a wash" against gold-100, so gold-100 stays the working set (07-29). Judges and generators: "try haiku first then, and we can do this headless in the same way?" (07-16), "we decided to use haiku for the fucking evals also" (07-29), against his standing complaints about qwen's speed.

§9 what the score is NOT for — the clearest statement in the whole record, [CHAT] 07-25: "what the fuck is it with you agents and the absurde insane fucking need to 'chase the highest number' i have fucking nowhere said or hinted that a high … score on something is the fucking target and point of this. the fucking POINT, is that the ARTEFACT, is academically VALID according to WHAT THE FUCK I AM TRYING TO BUILD". The score is a measurement of an artefact whose validity is the objective; it is not the objective.

§10–13. §10 aggregation and multi-hop: "but, doesnt the graph give actual relational connections to things like this, i mean, if the 'name' example you had, why wouldnt if just find all of those names? i dont get it" ([DOC] 06-28 [t33]) — and the reading that the aggregation path (interpreter classifies the prompt shape, then structural scope → semantic filter → full recall with no cap → group-by chunk attribute → count/max → directory join) was designed in full on 06-28 and 07-01 and never built. §11 relationships and hub nodes, and its REVERSAL — hard fields: attributes, then nodes/edges, then rejected as SQL schema: on 06-12 he ruled shared fields onto chunks as attributes, on the argument that node-ifying them creates edges to every chunk and near-duplicate nodes; on 06-30/07-01 he reopened it and asked for nodes and edges because "half the strength of of a graph is beeing able to route/search based on relationships instead of structures"; and on 08-02 he rejected the concrete hub-node build onto herb-eval as "dude, you are turbo-overfitting now, AND doing shit that might as well be sql-schema". §12 generalization beyond HERB, in his own words on 07-30: indexing finds structures → graph → retrieval, auto-fitted per dataset; and "Dont think herb, think dataset agnostic concept" (07-01). §13 weights — measured, never emitted: the rule that the model emits no numbers, ever, tagger and interpreter both, is recorded on 06-11 as a user ruling in the doc's own wording rather than his, with "it took so fucking long to get it right and it still didn't work at all" as his stated evidence — and it is contradicted at HEAD by the arm actually under test, whose interpreter emits facet values 0.0–1.0 at query time.

PART II — the working-relationship canon, §14–23. §14 do not manufacture canon: three separate documented incidents of agent output being mistaken for canon are recorded inside the design docs themselves — 05-31 fabricated memory files, 06-11 the leaked axis apparatus, 06-25 the memories and DESIGN.md found to misrepresent the facet model — and a statement being written down is not his approval of it: "you create an item and then suddenly think it's canon just because YOU fucking named it so" (07-25). §15 an opinion is not a command and a question is not a work order: "Me having a fucking opinion will NEVER be a fucking command", and trust revoked after an agent implemented and pushed an accidental plan (07-16). §16 communication, including the context rule (07-16): he is always speaking against the latest exchange, and the answer is short, plain and in spoken English. §17 he runs the scripts and the terminal must show life. §18 usage is finite and he pays for it, with the full account of how it went wrong on 07-25 after the three usage burns. §19 reusable tools, not a new script per experiment. §20 delegation and adversarial review: the adversarial-panel idea (07-22), orchestrator mode (07-22), the blind control he ordered run (07-22), and the three shipping-gate adversaries — academic rigor, senior engineer, overfitting/leakage (07-23). §21 read the actual thing — code, git, repo — not a summary of it. §22 repo, commits, and what must never be thrown away, with his commit style short, lower-case and human, no AI footers on any commit he wrote himself. §23 machine and environment facts he stated himself.

PART III — the dated timeline of decisions and reversals, one quote-anchored line each with ↺ marking a reversal of something earlier in the list, running 05-07 → 08-03. Its shape: the project starts fully designed (05-07); the cluster dimensions are renamed to the five words still in use (05-11); quarantine-don't-delete (05-14); the v2 pivot and "no hard filters anywhere" (05-30/31); chunk-as-coherent-episode with the cap as a calibration seed (06-03/04); weights measured from geometry, never emitted (06-09); ↺ the chunk description killed and ↺ the axis/projection apparatus killed as never-his, plus THE BUILD GATE (06-11); the spine closes (06-12); the thesis is done (06-14); ↺ RAGAS only, seven days after "we do both", and "MY WORDS ARE THE CANON", and ↺ tag-facets separated from routing (06-25); ↺ facets as graded relevance dials two days later (06-27);
